data.narrative:
Osaro is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Derik Pridmore and Michael Kahane that has raised $86.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (277810.KQ), with three primary private peers in the same sector and stage: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression approach applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $87M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $165M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of the three same-sector, same-stage comparables at $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range of $140M to $2.0B, with a median of $957M. The disparity reflects fundamental uncertainty about Osaro's positioning relative to established peers. The stage-progression method assumes capital deployed tracks value creation linearly; the peer-median method assumes market-validated pricing of comparable-stage robotics companies applies. Reconciliation would require clarity on Osaro's revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and technical differentiation relative to Bedrock Robotics and Dexterity. The $140M–$2.0B range brackets plausible outcomes but underscores that peer comparability assumptions drive the majority of valuation variance.
